AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To compare functional outcomes of acute inpatient rehabilitation for spinal epidural abscess (SEA) patients with and without history of intravenous substance abuse (IVSA).

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: Retrospective case series study in freestanding rehabilitation hospital.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Charts of 28 SEA patients admitted from 01/2012 to 9/2015: 13 with IVSA and 15 without IVSA were reviewed. Both groups received standard-of-care rehabilitation. Statistical analyses of Functional Independence Measure (FIM) scores were conducted using individual 2 (substance use) X 2 (rehabilitation status) repeated measures analysis of variance (ANOVA). Functional outcomes were defined by total FIM scores as well as motor and cognitive subsets. Length of stay (LOS) and morphine equivalents were also compared.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: There were no significant differences between the 2 groups. There was a significant main effect of treatment on total FIM scores (P<.001), FIM motor scores (P<.001), and FIM cognitive scores (P<.01) from admission to discharge. Subsequent student t-tests revealed that the scores of both groups significantly improved on all FIM components. There were no group differences on LOS and morphine equivalents at discharge.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Acute inpatient rehabilitation can effectively improve functional outcomes in SEA patients with or without IVSA, even though these 2 patient groups can vary in clinical factors.
